Victor, thank you for the time. Before the budget review, I want to make sure we are on the same page. You got the pre-read, didn't you?
I did. I read it on the plane. The adoption numbers are good, aren't they?
They are. Forty-eight stores are live, and that is ahead of the plan. Let me run through the three key numbers.
Please be quick. The board will only ask one question: what is the bottom line?
The bottom line is simple: each store saves about four hours a week. That is a strong number, isn't it?
It is. And the price for next year? Just give me a ballpark.

Hi Patrícia, it is Karen. Before the Brightwave budget review, remember the golden rule: the big meeting is not the place for surprises. Nobody should hear a number for the first time there. So book a short call with Victor this week, and send him a one-page pre-read two days before the call. On the call, check that you agree, but do not push. Question tags are perfect for this. You say: the numbers look good, don't they? And then you let him answer. If he says no, great: you found the problem before the meeting, not in it. And please do a dry run with me on Thursday. Fifteen minutes is enough.

Hi Patrícia, it is Daniel. Victor told me about your call. Thank you for looping me in. Two things before the meeting. First, the board likes short answers, so prepare three talking points and no more. Second, they will ask about the outage in August, won't they? I think you should mention it before they do. Say what happened, what you changed, and show them the new alert. If you say it first, it sounds like control. If they ask first, it sounds like a secret. See you on Monday.
